questions.stem: Which operator sends data to cout?
questions.solution: The insertion operator << writes to an output stream.

questions.stem: Which keyword prevents a variable's value from being changed after initialisation?
Which phase of the program development life cycle defines what the program must do?
questions.solution: Analysis establishes the requirements before design and coding.

questions.stem: Which part of a for loop is executed after each iteration?
questions.solution: The update expression runs after each iteration.

options: Translates the whole source program before execution
Executes one source statement at a time
questions.solution: A compiler translates the complete source file into object code.

questions.stem: Which structure chooses between two alternative paths?
Which data type stores a whole number?
questions.solution: int stores whole numbers; float stores real values.

questions.stem: Which loop is guaranteed to execute its body at least once?
questions.solution: do...while tests the condition after the body.

options: Arrays whose elements at the same index are related
questions.solution: Related data is stored at the same index in each array.

questions.stem: Which values can a bool variable hold?
questions.solution: A bool holds true or false.

questions.stem: This question tests the program development life cycle.

parts.text: Define source code and object code.
parts.answer: Source code is the human-readable program text; object code is the machine-oriented output produced by a compiler.
parts.label: a

parts.text: Describe THREE stages of the program development life cycle.
parts.answer: Analysis (requirements), design (algorithm/flowchart), coding (implementation), testing (verification), maintenance (updates). Any three stages.
parts.solution: Award 1 mark for each correctly described stage.
parts.label: b

questions.stem: A program reads a positive integer N and calculates the sum and average of the numbers 1 to N.

parts.text: Draw a flowchart for the sum and average calculation.
parts.answer: Start -> read N -> total = 0, count = 1 -> while count <= N add count -> average = total / N -> display total and average -> end.
parts.solution: Award marks for input, initialisation, loop condition, accumulator, average and output.
parts.label: a

parts.text: Write pseudocode and a complete C++ program for the algorithm.
parts.answer: Use a for loop from 1 to N, accumulate total, compute average as double(total)/N, then display both values.
parts.solution: Award marks for loop, accumulator, correct average type and output.
parts.label: b

questions.stem: This question tests declarations, constants and expressions.

parts.text: Write C++ declarations for: an integer age, a double price, a constant discount rate of 0.10 and a character grade.
parts.answer: int age; double price; const double DISCOUNT = 0.10; char grade;
parts.solution: Award marks for correct types, names and const initialisation.
parts.label: a

parts.text: Write C++ statements to read age and price, calculate price after discount, and display the result.
parts.answer: cin >> age >> price; price = price - price * DISCOUNT; cout << price;
parts.solution: Award marks for input, discount expression and output.
parts.label: b

parts.text: Trace the program and state the output.
parts.label: a

parts.text: Rewrite the segment using a do...while loop that sums only values greater than 5.
parts.answer: int i=0,s=0; do { if(a[i]>5) s+=a[i]; i++; } while(i<5); cout<<s;
parts.solution: Award marks for do...while, condition, filter and output.
parts.label: b

questions.stem: A class records ten student marks in an array.

parts.text: Declare an integer array of ten marks and read the marks from the user.
parts.answer: int marks[10]; for(int i=0;i<10;i++) cin >> marks[i];
parts.solution: Award marks for array declaration, loop and input.
parts.label: a

parts.text: Write a program segment to calculate and display the average, highest mark and number of marks above the average.
parts.answer: Compute total and highest in one loop; average = double(total)/10; then second loop counts marks > average.
parts.solution: Award marks for total, average, highest, second loop and output.
parts.label: b

questions.stem: A catering company charges RM12.50 per meal. Orders of 50-99 meals cost RM11.50 each, 100-199 cost RM10.50 each, and 200 or more cost RM9.50 each.
questions.solution: Award 3 marks for input/validation, 6 for price selection and total, 3 for repetition, 2 for final totals and 1 for output clarity.

parts.text: Write a complete C++ program that reads the customer name and quantity, validates the quantity, calculates the total, displays a receipt, and repeats until the user chooses to stop. At the end, display the total quantity and total sales.
parts.solution: Award 3 marks for input/validation, 6 for price selection and total, 3 for repetition, 2 for final totals and 1 for output clarity.

questions.stem: A bookstore records up to five books. Each book has a title, price and quantity in stock.
questions.solution: Award 3 marks for struct definition, 4 for input, 4 for inventory value, 3 for most expensive and 1 for output.

parts.text: Define a struct Book. Write a complete C++ program that reads the records, calculates the total inventory value, and displays the title of the most expensive book.
parts.solution: Award 3 marks for struct definition, 4 for input, 4 for inventory value, 3 for most expensive and 1 for output.
